config.text: APNEP Data Inventory Conflicts Viewer
Pressure (purple) × Resource (green) — dark indigo marks the highest-conflict cells. Use "Show conflict hotspots" to see only those.

Conflict pairs map the spatial overlap between human-use pressures and ecological or community resources across the Albemarle-Pamlico region, on a ~5 km² hex grid with a 3×3 bivariate classification.


Pressure:

Human use or stressors: vessel traffic, fishing, tourism, agriculture, roads and ferries, shoreline erosion, community vulnerability.


Resource:

Habitat, community value, or supply: submerged aquatic vegetation, nursery areas, wetlands, conservation areas.


How to use:

Pick a category, then a pressure–resource pairing. Each side panel shows that pair's profile and how to read it. Use the filter buttons (High Pressure / High Resources / High Conflict Zones) to keep only those cells.


Colors:

Dark indigo cells — conflict hotspots (both axes High).

Muddy / mixed colors — both axes at least Medium.

Cells with no data on either side are not shown.


Pair comparison:

  • Community Vulnerability x Conservation — data 94.3% · conflict 5.4% (the hottest pair)
  • Community Vulnerability x Tourism — data 93.6% · conflict 0.1%
  • Agriculture x Salinity — data 83.8% · conflict 0.2%
  • Shoreline Erosion x Wetland Potential — data 73.8% · conflict 0.8%
  • Vessel Count x Submerged Aquatic Vegetation — data 14.0% · conflict 0.1%
  • Fishing x Nursery Areas — data 13.7% · conflict 0.2%
  • Sea Level Rise x Ferry Route — data 3.5% · conflict 0.0%


Method notes:

Layers are aggregated per hex in EPSG:32119, classified into Low / Medium / High terciles on non-zero cells, and exported in WGS84. Data are provided without warranty; users are responsible for using the data in a manner consistent with the limitations of geospatial data.

config.text:
Fishing x Nursery Areas


Pressure — Commercial Fishing:

VMS (Vessel Monitoring System — satellite tracking of commercial fishing vessels) density 2015–2019 (Northeast Ocean Data), mean density class per cell.


Resource — Nursery Areas:

NC Fishery Nursery Areas designation (NC Division of Marine Fisheries), % cell area covered.


Reading it: only a few cells combine high activity with nursery coverage — the closure system is largely working. Watch the band of activity pressed against nursery boundaries.


Pair profile:

Data coverage — 13.7% of cells

High pressure — 27.9% of data cells

High resource — 8.2% of data cells

Conflict (both High) — 0.2% of data cells


Colors:

Dark indigo cells — conflict hotspots (both axes High).

Muddy / mixed colors — both axes at least Medium.

Cells with no data on either side are not shown.

Vessel Count x Submerged Aquatic Vegetation


Pressure — Vessel Count:

AIS (Automatic Identification System — transponder tracking of vessels) transit counts 2025 (Northeast Ocean Data Portal), summed per cell.


Resource — Submerged Aquatic Vegetation (SAV):

SAV (submerged aquatic vegetation — underwater grass beds) mapping 2019–2020 (NC Dept. of Environmental Quality), % cell area covered.


Reading it: the darkest cells mark shipping lanes and ferry corridors crossing SAV beds — priority zones for speed restrictions, signage, or channel review.

Cells with no data on either side are not shown.

Community Vulnerability x Conservation


Pressure — Community Vulnerability:

CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) 2022 — higher score means a more vulnerable community; mean percentile per cell.


Resource — Conservation:

PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the U.S.) 4.1 protected lands (GAP 1–3), % cell area covered.


Reading it: the darkest cells are protected lands overlapping high-vulnerability communities — the engagement priority list for access agreements, stewardship, and Tribal / local consultation.

Community Vulnerability x Tourism


Pressure — Community Vulnerability:

CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) 2022, mean percentile per cell — the demand side.


Resource — Tourism:

NC beach and waterfront public access points, count per cell — the supply side.


Reading it: the darkest cells are vulnerable communities with heavy tourist access — congestion and displacement hotspots. High vulnerability with few access points marks the resident-access gap.

Shoreline Erosion x Wetland Potential


Pressure — Shoreline Erosion:

NC oceanfront erosion rates 2020 (NC Division of Coastal Management), eroding shoreline km per cell.


Resource — Wetland Potential:

NOAA C-CAP (Coastal Change Analysis Program) wetland potential layer, land wetness likelihood 1–9 (open water excluded).


Reading it: the darkest cells are eroding shorefront backed by high wetland-migration potential — priority candidates for living shorelines and shoreline-hardening policy review.

Agriculture x Salinity


Pressure — Salinity:

Estuarine shoreline length per cell (NC DCM 2012), used as a proxy for the saltwater front.


Resource — Agriculture:

NLCD (National Land Cover Database) 2025 cropland — pasture + cultivated crops, % cell area.


Reading it: the darkest cells are the salt front pressing against farmland — where intrusion risk to agriculture is highest.

Sea Level Rise x Ferry Route


Pressure — Sea Level Rise:

NOAA sea level rise inundation footprint (Northern + Middle 2 NC), % cell area covered.


Resource — Ferry Route:

U.S. DOT ferry routes + terminals, route length (km) and terminal count per cell.


Reading it: the darkest cells mark ferry corridors crossing inundation footprints — priorities for terminal elevation, docking retrofit, and service contingency planning.
